title: Wood Mackenzie analysts explain fundamental paradox of US solar supply chain
notes: 'Record imports in 2023 and 2024 created sufficient inventory to sustain US demand through 2025. However, this buffer is depleting rapidly.'

title: Solar and storage supply chain dashboard
notes: US module capacity 14.5 GW (end 2023) → 42.1 (end 2024) → 65.5 (end 2025) → ~66 (Q2 2026); 75.3 GW operational on SEIA's dashboard method.

publisher: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL)
notes: 2024: 13.0 GW of modules produced against 31.8 GW capacity (first-year utilisation ~20–45%); record imports 56.1 GWdc modules, 13.8 GWdc cells in 2024.

title: Department of Commerce issues final determination in circumvention inquiries
notes: Five of eight investigated companies found circumventing via Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam: evidence that blocked supply re-routes.

title: Solar Market Insight Report Q2 2025
notes: Imports from the four SE Asian countries fell after AD/CVD while Indonesia and Laos rose to 34.6% of module imports: roughly a quarter to a half of lost volume reappeared from other origins within quarters.

title: UFLPA enforcement FAQs

title: VSUN solar modules detained under UFLPA could knock US$30 million off company earnings
notes: 'The overwhelming majority of these products (79%) were ultimately released'; long tails for contested cases (Maxeon detained from July 2024, excluded).

title: BNEF Tier 1 solar module manufacturers: methodology
notes: Bankability (Tier 1) requires modules in six bank-financed projects within two years: a proxy for how long a new supplier takes to be accepted.
